glossary.Hyperaemic: Red and engorged with extra blood flow.
glossary.Pus: Thick fluid of dead white cells and bacteria from infection.
glossary.Malaise: A general feeling of being unwell.
glossary.Anterior cervical lymphadenopathy: Enlarged lymph nodes in the front of the neck.
glossary.WCC: White cell count; raised in bacterial infection.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, a blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.Tonsillar capsule: The fibrous layer surrounding each tonsil.
glossary.Pharyngeal muscles: The constrictor muscles of the throat wall.
glossary.Peritonsillar space: The tissue space between the tonsil capsule and the throat muscles.
glossary.Peritonsillar mass: A swelling beside the tonsil, usually pus in quinsy.
glossary.Erythromycin: A macrolide antibiotic, an alternative for penicillin allergy.
glossary.Azithromycin: A macrolide antibiotic taken once daily, an alternative for penicillin allergy.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs used to reduce swelling.
glossary.Adjunct: An extra treatment given alongside the main one.
glossary.Drainage: Letting pus out, by needle aspiration or incision.
glossary.Statin: A cholesterol-lowering drug such as atorvastatin.
glossary.Lymphoid tissue: Tissue packed with lymphocytes that fights infection, such as tonsils and lymph nodes.
glossary.Virulence factors: Molecules a microbe uses to infect and damage the host.
glossary.Self-care: Managing symptoms at home with rest, fluids and simple painkillers.
glossary.Dehydrated: Short of body water, for example from not drinking.
glossary.Systemically unwell: Ill throughout the body, not just locally, such as with high fever, lethargy or poor fluid intake.
glossary.Foul breath: Bad-smelling breath, from anaerobic infection or pus.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used for pain, fever and inflammation.
glossary.Muffled voice: Dull, thick-sounding voice caused by swelling in the throat.
